title: Animal Volley: AI helped build the artwork, but visual consistency took repeated corrections
author: Paxstudio
selftext:
I’m the developer behind Animal Volley, a released Android arcade volleyball game. Think of the short rallies in Blobby Volley, with animal characters, a three-skill reserve, and online friend matches. This is my own game, so I’m marking the post as commercial self-promotion; it is free with optional rewarded ads.



One useful lesson from making it with AI tools was that generating more assets did not automatically improve consistency. A 3D/Godot experiment moved too far away from the original character designs, so I paused that direction and kept the original game. Promotional video generation had its own problem: the cat kept taking off its hood between shots. Simplifying the action and tightening the reference helped more than adding bigger effects.



AI-assisted coding still needed repeated in-game checks. We corrected the character scale in online matches, spike inputs, localized text overflowing wooden UI frames, and low-end performance. The trailer below combines gameplay with promotional animation; it is not all raw gameplay.



For this project, reviewing actual screens and motion mattered more than whether a generated image looked good by itself. I’m sharing the result and that experience here, rather than a claim that the workflow was one-click.



Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.animal.volley1&hl=en](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.animal.volley1&hl=en)
